title: CSIS Launches Commission on Future Transatlantic Relations
text:
CSIS Launches Commission on Future Transatlantic Relations

Press Release

— November 20, 2026

WASHINGTON, DC – November 20, 2026 – The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) today announced the launch of the Commission on Future Transatlantic Relations (CFTR), a new initiative led by the CSIS Europe, Russia, and Eurasia Program to recalibrate and strengthen the United States’ strategic approach to Europe.Set to launch in January 2027, the commission will include leading Europe experts, policy practitioners, and business leaders, with the goal of building a framework for a transatlantic relationship that is stronger, more resilient, and more prosperous for allies on both sides of the Atlantic.“For too long, U.S. policy toward Europe has relied on the status quo rather than a strategy,” said Max Bergmann, director of the CSIS Europe, Russia, and Eurasia Program. “As Europe’s role in the world evolves, this commission will define the partnership the United States wants with Europe and what it will take to achieve it.”Through the CFTR, members will spend one year conducting targeted research focused on four key issue areas: the fundamentals of U.S. engagement with Europe, defense and burden sharing, technology and digital infrastructure, and the transatlantic economic agenda.The initiative will be chaired by Ambassador Julianne Smith, president of Clarion Strategies and former U.S. permanent representative to NATO; Ambassador John J. Sullivan, distinguished fellow at the Georgetown University School of Foreign Service, former U.S. ambassador to Russia, and former deputy secretary of state; and Ambassador Mark Brzezinski, president and CEO of Brzezinski Global Strategies and former U.S. ambassador to Sweden and Poland.“This is a transformative moment for the transatlantic relationship. Many of the assumptions that held it together for decades are being tested, both from within and from without,” said Amb. Smith. “Restating our commitment won’t be enough to meet this moment. We need to look at the transatlantic bargain with fresh eyes and reimagine it for the decades ahead. That is the work of the CFTR, and I’m proud to serve as a co-chair.”“The transatlantic relationship is the anchor for America’s engagement with the world,” said Amb. Brzezinski. “I am delighted to join my colleagues to advance the unity of purpose and shared values around which the transatlantic relationship was founded, and build a shared approach to the challenges of our time.”“The transatlantic relationship is as vital as ever,” said Amb. Sullivan. “Yet as the geopolitical and technological challenges we face become more acute, it is equally vital that the relationship adapts to meet the needs of a new future. I look forward to working with my colleagues to address these needs.”Learn more about the CSIS Europe, Russia, and Eurasia Program here.For media inquiries, please contact press@csis.org.
